examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.

meanings.note: Used as conjunction (그렇지만).

examples.text: 역시 우리 신디는 똑똑해. 그렇지만 신디야, 난 잃어봤단다.
examples.trans: Smart as ever, our Cindy—except Cindy, I have already lost a star like you once before.

examples.text: 너처럼 나한텐 소중한 아이였어. 그렇지만 그 아이를 잃고 나니까 네가 왔잖니?
examples.trans: She was just as precious to me as you are—yet right after I lost her, you came along, remember?

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.note: Used to emphasize an adjective or verb.

examples.trans: It's really pretty.
I'm truly sorry.

meanings.en: actually, in fact, to tell the truth
meanings.note: adverbial use of the noun 사실 (fact)

examples.trans: Honestly, I don't know well either.
In fact, I couldn't sleep yesterday.

meanings.note: Written as one word (한번) when softening a suggestion or request ('why don't we...').

examples.trans: Try eating this food.
Come visit sometime when you have time.

meanings.note: noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.
I want to even try right now.
How about trying to even try together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 여기서 대기하다가 본부장님 미사 끝나시면 성당 앞으로 모시러 가야 돼.
examples.trans: I am waiting on standby here, and once the division head finishes Mass, I have to pick him up in front of the cathedral.
This expression comes from 'waiting on standby and then'.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Used as causal -아서 (생각나서).

examples.text: 저희 어머님은 가수 전영록 씨 노래를 들으면 아직도 옛날 연애하던 좋았던 시절이 생각나서 가슴이 떨리고 좋으시답니다.
examples.trans: Whenever my mother hears singer Jeon Young-rok's songs, her heart still flutters happily remembering the sweet days when she was young and in love.

examples.text: 이제는 놀이공원 하면 피디님 생각날 것 같아.
examples.trans: From now on, whenever someone mentions an amusement park, I think I will remember you, Producer.
I want to humbly tell him right now.
How about trying to humbly tell him together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this since I intend to?
I was busy today because of since I intend to.
Did you hear about this filming too?
I was busy today because of filming too.
See you at the shoot!

examples.text: 저도 뵌 적은 없어요, 늘 우리 신디를 통해서 듣기만 했죠.
examples.trans: I have never met them in person either—I always only heard about them through our Cindy.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
